top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson (P001) is my first choice on the work. From public knowledge, not fresh reading or independent verification, her voice is distinctive and her formal invention carries the thought: Autobiography of Red recasts a fragmentary Greek source as a modern verse novel, Nox makes elegy into a book whose form is part of the mourning, and the essays on eros extend the same practice of making an inherited form carry present grief and desire. The citation should be scoped to original poetry, verse novel and essay and anchored in the printed text, with the classical versions as context and Nox's physical form as an extension I cannot fully judge. I can read her in the original, which lowers one uncertainty but does not add merit. The case rests on a handful of titles, and whether her later and more performance-oriented work sustains that level is unverified. Cărtărescu (P002) is a close second, with a more compact project and larger scale. His case depends on translation of the Romanian and on whether the late novels extend or repeat the earlier work, and neither can be tested here. The difference is one of weighting, between breadth of formal reinvention and unity of a single project, and it is not decisive. I rank both above no award (P000) because each shows sustained voice and depth within the framework of Nobel's will. Opening and proposal support counts are not evidence of merit.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; the profile records no tie to any shortlisted writer, and his Dagens Nyheter criticism was not surveyed, so earlier reviews of a shortlisted writer cannot be ruled out. His own documentary historical fiction is context only, not evidence of preference.
